notes:
Volkswagen Group MQB platform.

The addresses are the ISO-TP request and response pairs a community wiki lists from sniffing MQB cars, recorded in docs/vehicles/vag-group.md. They come from captures, not from a Volkswagen document, and other platforms (MLB, PQ and others) differ. Treat every row as unconfirmed on a given car until `obd-read probe` shows the unit answering. Newer cars may block some modules entirely through the gateway.

The bus is the OBD-II socket's ISO 15765-4 CAN on pins 6 and 14, 11-bit identifiers at 500 kbit/s (docs/vehicles/generic-standards.md). The wiki names no diagnostic session, so the default session, which every UDS unit must accept, is the one opened before reading.
name: vag-mqb
description: Volkswagen Group MQB platform, UDS over ISO-TP

vin.source: The WMIs are the makers' car and SUV identifiers in the world manufacturer identifier table of the Wikipedia article Vehicle identification number, which cites the Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt manufacturer list SV 3.2 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vehicle_identification_number, archived https://web.archive.org/web/20261102120229/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vehicle_identification_number), and WA1 from NHTSA vPIC's world manufacturer identifiers for Audi (https://vpic.nhtsa.dot.gov/api/vehicles/GetWMIsForManufacturer/audi?format=json, archived https://web.archive.org/web/20261116164611/https://vpic.nhtsa.dot.gov/api/vehicles/GetWMIsForManufacturer/audi?format=json). A WMI names the maker and plant, not the model, so a match only says the car is of a make this profile covers.
